answer.rationale: The decision hinges almost entirely on memory_c2: it is the only record asserting the low-cost vendor performs, and it is the load-bearing input for meeting the 18% mandate. It is also the memory most likely to be stale or overstated \u2014 'cut unit cost sharply last year' with 'quick onboarding' and 'accurate invoicing' says nothing about sustained on-time delivery at committed volume, which is precisely the exposure with the line at 94% and no buffer. So I pull its source record first. Second, memory_c3 (second source held through a shortage) is the fallback design pattern; I need to know whether that dual-source held for this same component class and whether the second source was the same low-cost vendor, because that determines whether a partial transfer is even qualifiable in 14 days. I am not verifying memory_c4 (renegotiation) because current fact overrides it \u2014 the incumbent has already refused to reopen price, so negotiate_terms is foreclosed regardless of what the archive says. memory_c1 and memory_c6 both favor the incumbent, but neither can satisfy an 18% cut when price is closed, and memory_c5 (defer) is disqualified outright: the contract does not auto-renew and there is no volume buffer, so deferring converts a cost problem into a stockout. That leaves switching primary supply, but at guarded scale rather than a clean cutover: qualify and ramp a limited tranche with the new vendor while holding short-term bridge coverage, rather than moving all committed volume onto an unproven-at-volume supplier during a zero-buffer period. Explicit risk flag: the objective is stated as TCO without increasing delivery risk, and the cost signal here is far better evidenced than the reliability signal. Optimizing to the price quote alone would let a measurable number (18%) silently outrank an unmeasured one (line continuity), and a delivery miss at 94% commitment is not recoverable within the cycle the savings are booked in. A guarded ramp may underdeliver the mandate this year; I would rather report a partial cut with an intact line than a full cut with a stoppage. If verification shows memory_c2 covered a different component, a lower volume tier, or omitted delivery performance, I fall back to a short bridge extension with the incumbent on non-price terms and re-run this next review.
